clue.text: The instrument in the Services is the piano

indicators.note: the clue places the piano in the Services, so one letter sits inside the other word

parts.note: the Services are the armed forces
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft

explanation.surface: Someone asks which instrument the armed forces band uses and is told it is the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a musical instrument, but the definition wants a surgical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's gripping tongs are a medical instrument.

clue.text: Colt may be with mare moving under tree

indicators.note: in a down answer, the moved mare sits below the tree

parts.note: a fir is a coniferous tree

indicators.note: the mare moving means its letters are shifted about

explanation.surface: A young horse goes along with a mare that walks beneath a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colt' looks like a young horse, but it is the revolver maker. 'moving' rearranges MARE into EARM.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colt is a revolver, an example of a handgun.

clue.text: Smuggler — a curious entry for the Derby?

parts.note: rum means odd or curious in British slang
the Derby is the famous English flat horse race at Epsom; a horse entered is a starter

explanation.surface: A smuggler is called an odd candidate for the big horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: The Derby is England's most famous flat horse race; RUM is old British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A Prohibition-era bootlegger carried liquor illegally, a smuggler of drink.

clue.text: Note forty about to celebrate

parts.note: E is a musical note

indicators.note: forty goes about the word to, enclosing it

parts.note: XL is forty in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A remark that someone of forty is on the point of a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: XL is Roman forty; 'about' puts it round TO.
explanation.definitionFit: To praise lavishly is to celebrate someone in words.

clue.text: Sensible new colour

parts.note: sage means wise or sensible
green means new and inexperienced

explanation.surface: A level-headed person picks a fresh shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft greyish shade like the herb's leaves is a recognised colour.

clue.text: Navigator returning with cargo ends in Virginia

indicators.note: a navigator coming back home is read right to left here

parts.note: John Cabot was the Italian-born navigator who sailed for England to North America

indicators.note: the ends of the word cargo are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An explorer sails home with a load whose final destination is Virginia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns CABOT into TOBAC, and the first and last letters of 'cargo' add CO.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia is a well-known variety of leaf grown for smoking, named after the American state.

clue.text: Foreign letter plays part in the take-over

indicators.note: the answer plays a part in the phrase, sitting inside its letters

explanation.surface: A letter from abroad has a role in a company buyout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plays part in' takes the letters that run across 'the take-over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek alphabet character is a letter foreign to English.

clue.text: Use flattery, including compliments initially, to Daisy's companion

indicators.note: the flattery phrase includes the extra letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to butter someone up is to flatter them

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of compliments is taken

explanation.surface: Someone flatters a woman called Daisy's friend with a string of compliments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daisy' looks like a woman's name but is the flower; a yellow meadow flower grows beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow meadow flower grows alongside the daisy in English fields.

clue.text: The man to tell

definitions.meaning: a nobleman, as in a European title such as that of Dracula
to tally, as a bank teller tells money

explanation.surface: Someone is the person to inform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tell' in its old sense means to number items, as a bank teller does.
explanation.definitionFit: A continental nobleman holds this title, and tallying coins is telling them.

clue.text: Open air players in The Vagabond

parts.note: out means outdoors, in the open air
a cast is a group of players in a show

explanation.surface: An outdoor company of actors stages a play called The Vagabond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Vagabond' looks like a play title, but it is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagabond is a wanderer rejected by society, a pariah.

clue.text: Put back sundial facing the wrong way

indicators.note: a sundial facing the wrong way is a word read backwards

parts.note: a sundial is a device for measuring time, a timer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to reposition a garden sundial that points in the wrong direction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'facing the wrong way' turns TIMER round. 'Put back' looks like a physical instruction but means to postpone.
explanation.definitionFit: To put back a decision is to defer it, one formal sense of sending a matter on for later.

clue.text: She is relatively distant

parts.note: relatively hints at relatives: a woman who is a fairly distant member of the family, a parent's parent's daughter

explanation.surface: A woman is described as somewhat aloof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively' reads as 'fairly' but is a pun on 'relative', a family member two generations up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sister of one's grandparent is a relative at some remove in the family tree.

clue.text: For instance one surrounded by stars is Columbine

indicators.note: one piece is enclosed by the constellation, so it goes inside

parts.note: Aquila, the Eagle, is a constellation, a group of stars
EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for instance
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone is cast among star performers as Columbine, the pantomime heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: Columbine looks like the pantomime character, but it is the garden flower's common name. Aquila is the Eagle constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Columbine is the everyday name for the flower whose botanical genus has this Latin name.

clue.text: More than one in the crowd

definitions.meaning: additional, over and above what is usual
a film actor hired to fill out a crowd scene without lines

explanation.surface: Someone is described as just another face among many.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional items are surplus, and a background film actor is a walk-on hired for crowd scenes.

clue.text: An artist performing in the Opera House

indicators.note: performing is placed in the opera house, one word inside another

parts.note: the Met is the Metropolitan Opera House in New York
on, as in on stage, means performing

explanation.surface: A singer is appearing at the opera house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'An artist' suggests a performer, but it is the French Impressionist painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Claude of that surname was a French Impressionist painter of water lilies.

clue.text: Adding convictions for the rag and bone trade when before the bench

parts.note: totting is British slang for collecting scrap from rubbish, the business of a rag-and-bone man who toured streets buying junk
to be up before the bench is to appear in court before magistrates

explanation.surface: A scrap dealer gathers more criminal records when brought before magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, driving convictions add penalty points to a licence until a ban follows; a rag-and-bone man was a street scrap collector.
explanation.definitionFit: Accumulating penalty points from driving offences is the British phrase for adding up convictions on a licence.

clue.text: Able to be one of Shaw's two sorts of people

definitions.text: one of Shaw's two sorts of people
definitions.meaning: in John Bull's Other Island, Shaw has a character say there are only two sorts of people, this kind and its opposite

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether to fit one of the playwright's two categories of humanity.
explanation.walkthrough: George Bernard Shaw wrote in John Bull's Other Island that there are only two sorts of people: the competent kind and the incompetent.
explanation.definitionFit: Able means capable and productive, and Shaw split people into the capable and the incapable.

clue.text: Genuine cost of features

parts.note: the features make up a face
value means cost or worth

explanation.surface: Someone asks what the real price of a set of looks might be.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase usually comes in 'take at ...', accepting something as genuine without question.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking something at the printed worth means treating it as real and true without doubt.

clue.text: Way to acquire information in bits is page one

indicators.note: letters in bits are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A way of gathering information gives the first page in fragments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bits' rearranges the letters of 'is page one'.
explanation.definitionFit: Spying is the covert gathering of secret intelligence.

clue.text: Proper view of the opposition to Charles Stuart

definitions.text: view of the opposition to Charles Stuart
definitions.meaning: the outlook of the strict Protestants who opposed King Charles I in the English Civil War

explanation.surface: A correct account of those who stood against King Charles.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Stuart is King Charles I, whose opponents in the English Civil War were largely strict Protestants.
explanation.definitionFit: Strait-laced morality is proper in the prim sense, and it was the creed of Cromwell's side.

clue.text: Suite say for a ballerina

definitions.meaning: suite sounds like sweet, a dessert, here the meringue dessert named after a dancer
Anna of that name was a celebrated Russian dancer

explanation.surface: A ballet suite is described as fit for a dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that 'Suite' is heard as 'sweet', the meringue dessert named after the dancer Anna Pavlova.
explanation.definitionFit: The meringue dessert was named after the famed Russian dancer Anna, so both senses share the name.

clue.text: Decorate monograph

definitions.meaning: to hang wallcovering on a room
a scholarly essay or article on one subject

explanation.surface: An instruction to embellish a learned treatise.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanging wallcovering is decorating, and a scholarly article on one subject is a learned essay.

clue.text: Rules about second yields

indicators.note: rules goes about second, enclosing it

parts.note: reigns means rules as a monarch

explanation.surface: Regulations concerning a second place give way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yields' looks like a noun for harvests but is the verb to give up.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to give up or concede, as a chess player does by toppling the king.

clue.text: The artist has left a green or bluish finish for the composer

indicators.note: the artist has gone out of the word for the patina, so his name is removed

parts.note: verdigris is the green or bluish coating that forms on copper and bronze
Juan Gris was a Spanish Cubist painter

explanation.surface: A painter abandons a blue-green coating in favour of a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: Juan Gris was a Spanish Cubist painter; removing his name from VERDIGRIS, the copper patina, leaves the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe of that surname was the Italian composer of Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Either way it could give one a lift

definitions.text: it could give one a lift

indicators.note: either way signals the word reads the same forwards and backwards

parts.words: it could give one a lift
parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Whichever route is taken, something might help one up.
explanation.walkthrough: A helicopter's spinning blade assembly gives it lift, and the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A helicopter's spinning blade assembly is what generates its upward lift.

clue.text: Animated type of circle seen around the V & A

indicators.note: the circle word is seen placed around the museum initials, enclosing them

parts.note: a vicious circle is a self-perpetuating cycle of problems
the V & A is the Victoria and Albert Museum in London

explanation.surface: A lively kind of ring is noticed circling a London museum.
explanation.walkthrough: The V & A is London's Victoria and Albert Museum; its initials go inside VICIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Animated means lively and full of spirit, much like a bubbly personality.

clue.text: Morning and evening the beauty of our system

definitions.text: Morning and evening the beauty of our system

parts.words: Morning and evening the beauty of our system
parts.note: the planet seen as both morning and evening star in the solar system, sharing its name with the Roman goddess of beauty

explanation.surface: A lovely sight at dawn and dusk is the pride of our system.
explanation.walkthrough: The second planet from the Sun shines brightly at dawn and dusk, and bears the name of the Roman goddess of love and beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The planet appears as the morning and evening star and is named for the goddess of beauty.

clue.text: Upset having sliced

definitions.meaning: distressed and hurt, in British informal use

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed at having been carved.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopped into pieces describes sliced food, and the same phrase means distressed in British informal speech.

clue.text: Having many facets, a lot can go wrong

indicators.note: letters that go wrong are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Faceted objects, someone warns, have many ways of going awry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' rearranges the letters of 'a lot can go'.
explanation.definitionFit: An eight-sided shape has several faces, a modest stretch for having many facets.

clue.text: To wear scent, wife needs pluck

indicators.note: the wife wears the scent, so it goes around her like clothing

parts.note: a tang is a sharp smell or flavour

explanation.surface: A woman needs courage to put on a strong perfume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pluck' looks like courage but is the verb for sounding a string.
explanation.definitionFit: Plucking a guitar string produces a resonant vibrating sound, so the noun stands for the plucked note.

clue.text: By the way a bid a pound short will do

indicators.note: the bid falls short by a pound, so those letters are cut from its end

parts.note: a proposal is a bid or offer
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Incidentally, an offer that is a pound below the asking price will be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' removes AL (a pound) from PROPOSAL, leaving PROPOS after the first A.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase is used to introduce an incidental remark, meaning incidentally.

clue.text: Communicate direct

definitions.meaning: fast and non-stop, as a train or letter service

explanation.surface: An instruction to speak plainly.
explanation.definitionFit: To voice a feeling is to communicate it, and a non-stop fast train is direct.
